findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request cancellation
findings.body: `WithTimeoutCause` adds a deadline but keeps the request context as its parent. These REST calls return immediately after starting the goroutine, and the request context is canceled when request handling completes. Any legacy operation still in progress is therefore canceled on response, so the mode's mirror writes are unreliable. Detach the background context from request cancellation before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Independent goroutines can apply writes to legacy out of order
findings.body: Each write starts an independent goroutine, with no per-resource ordering. For example, a legacy update can run before the legacy create for the same object, fail with NotFound, and then the later create leaves legacy with stale data; a delayed create can similarly run after a delete and resurrect an object. The errors are not retried, so the stores can remain divergent. Serialize or otherwise order mirror writes per resource.

findings.title: Legacy updates are recomputed against the legacy copy instead of mirroring unified storage
findings.body: The goroutine passes the original `objInfo` to `Legacy.Update` rather than applying the object returned by unified storage. For patch or apply updates, legacy recomputes the result against its own old object; if that copy is stale, fields omitted from the patch can remain stale and the mirror will differ from the authoritative unified result. Mirror the computed unified object (as the previous update wrapper did) so both stores receive the same update.

findings.title: Mode 3 duration metrics use incorrect backend and resource values
findings.body: This storage-duration call passes the individual object `name` where the other calls pass `options.Kind`, creating a high-cardinality metric dimension as arbitrary resource names accumulate. The attribution is also inconsistent elsewhere: Create and Update record storage failures as legacy durations (lines 45 and 129), while the asynchronous legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded as a storage duration (line 166). These errors make backend metrics misleading and can cause excessive metric series.

findings.title: The mode 3 integration test assumes the asynchronous mirror is immediate
findings.body: This subtest invokes `doPlaylistTests`, which checks the legacy API immediately after Kubernetes create and update operations. Mode 3 returns before its legacy-write goroutines complete, so those assertions race the mirror and can fail intermittently. Poll for eventual convergence or synchronize the test with completion of the background writes.
